source.source_summary: Original relationship drama about a boyfriend secretly cancelling a couple's anniversary trip so he could use the refund to cover a personal financial mistake.

selected.title: He Cancelled Our Anniversary Trip Behind My Back
selected.hook: The airline agent asked why my boyfriend had cancelled both of our anniversary tickets.
selected.voiceover:
The airline agent asked why my boyfriend had cancelled both of our anniversary tickets.

I was calling because the app suddenly showed our flight as refunded. We were supposed to leave for Lisbon in four days, and my boyfriend had spent weeks talking about restaurants and beaches like nothing was wrong.

When I called him, he first blamed the airline.

Then I told him they had confirmed the cancellation came from his account.

He went quiet.

Apparently, three weeks earlier, he had lost almost two thousand dollars trying to flip concert tickets. His credit card payment was due, so he cancelled our trip and used the refund to cover it.

But that wasn't the part that got me.

He had already requested time off work, helped me buy luggage, and even asked me that morning what I wanted to do on our first night in Lisbon.

His plan was to wait until the day before the flight, pretend the airline had cancelled it, then suggest we postpone.

When I asked why he didn't just tell me about the money, he said he knew I'd be angry about the ticket scheme.

Exactly.

He wasn't hiding one bad decision. He built another lie around it and let me keep planning a trip that no longer existed.

Now he says cancelling a vacation shouldn't end a three-year relationship.

Would the lost trip bother you more, or the fact that he rehearsed the lie for weeks?
selected.youtube_description:
Four days before their anniversary trip to Lisbon, an airline call revealed that her boyfriend had secretly cancelled both tickets weeks earlier. The missing vacation was only the beginning of a money secret he had carefully planned to hide. Is one financial mistake forgivable when covering it requires weeks of lying?
